candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: duns
candidates.comment: A DUNS number relation between an organization or person and their Dun & Bradstreet DUNS identifier. Also called "DUNS identifier", "business ID". Examples: "Organization 'Acme Corp' duns '12-345-6789'", "Person 'Jane Doe' duns '98-765-4321'".

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: roofLoad
candidates.comment: The maximum permissible weight that can be carried on the roof of a vehicle, including cargo and any installations. Also called roof capacity, maximum roof weight, roof rack load limit. Examples: `SUV Model X` roofLoad `75 kg`, `Sedan Model Y` roofLoad `50 kg`, `Van Model Z` roofLoad `100 kg`. Distinct from `cargoVolume`, which refers to the internal cargo space.

candidates.label: vehicleSeatingCapacity
candidates.comment: A vehicle seating capacity relation between a vehicle and the number of passengers it can seat. Also called seating capacity, passenger capacity, number of seats. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '5'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '7 persons'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '2'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

candidates.label: cargoVolume
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement of the available volume for cargo or luggage in a vehicle. Also called "trunk volume", "luggage capacity", "storage volume". Examples: "Car vehicle cargoVolume 400 LTR", "Truck vehicle cargoVolume 100 FTQ".

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: vehicleIdentificationNumber
candidates.comment: A vehicle identification number relation between a vehicle and its unique serial number (VIN). Also called VIN, chassis number, serial number. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleIdentificationNumber '1G1AP52W691XXXXXX'", "Car vehicleIdentificationNumber 'JTDKN31V60JXXXXXX'", "Truck vehicleIdentificationNumber '3FAHP000000XXXXXX'".

candidates.label: vehicleInteriorType
candidates.comment: A vehicle interior type relation between a vehicle and the type or material of its interior. Also called interior material, upholstery type, cabin trim. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'synthetic fabric'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'wood trim'".

Examples: "A boat trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Port of Miami'.", "The ferry trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Dover Terminal'."

candidates.label: departureBoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port from which it departs. Also called: origin boat terminal, departure port, ferry terminal. Examples: "Ferry Trip" departure boat terminal "Dover Ferry Terminal", "Cruise" departure boat terminal "PortMiami". Distinct from arrivalBoatTerminal, which is the destination terminal.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: arrivalStation
candidates.comment: A station where a train trip concludes. Also called: train destination, end station, terminal station. Examples: "TrainTrip 456 arrivalStation 'Grand Central Station'", "TrainTrip from Rome arrivalStation 'Termini Station'", "TrainTrip to Berlin arrivalStation 'Hauptbahnhof'". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which specifies the specific platform within a station.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: arrivalAirport
candidates.comment: An arrival airport relation between a flight and the airport where it concludes. Also called destination airport, landing airport, final airport. Examples: "A flight's arrival airport is 'LAX'.", "The flight's arrival airport is 'Heathrow Airport'."

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: reservedTicket
candidates.comment: A ticket association between a reservation and the specific ticket for that reservation. Also called associated ticket, ticket for, ticket linked to. Examples: `Flight Reservation` reservedTicket `Boarding Pass #123`, `Concert Booking` reservedTicket `E-Ticket for Seat A12`, `Hotel Reservation` reservedTicket `Confirmation Ticket`.

candidates.label: pickupLocation
candidates.comment: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.

chosen_property.label: flewOver
chosen_property.definition: A vehicle flies over a geographical feature.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: flightNumber
candidates.comment: A flight number relation between a flight and its unique identifier, typically including the airline IATA code. Also called: flight ID, airline code, flight identifier. Examples: "Flight from London to New York" flight number "BA177", "Flight from Tokyo to San Francisco" flight number "UA838", "Flight from Sydney to Dubai" flight number "EK413".

candidates.label: flightDistance
candidates.comment: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

candidates.label: mealService
candidates.comment: A meal service relation between a flight and the description of meals provided or available for purchase. Also called: in-flight meals, catering options, food service. Examples: "Flight BA249 mealService 'Complimentary hot meal and beverages'", "Flight AA123 mealService 'Snacks and drinks available for purchase'", "Flight LH456 mealService 'Vegetarian option available upon request'".

candidates.label: departureTerminal
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.

candidates.label: departureGate
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure gate identifier. Also called: gate number, boarding gate, flight gate. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure gate "Gate A12", "Flight UA123" departure gate "Gate 34B". Distinct from arrivalGate, which is the arrival gate.

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration
candidates.comment: An estimated flight duration relation between a flight and the duration or text representing its approximate travel time. Also called "approximate flight time", "expected flight length", "scheduled flight duration". Examples: "Flight 'UA123' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT5H30M'", "Flight 'DL456' estimatedFlightDuration '6 hours'", "Flight 'LH789' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT10H'".

candidates.label: carrier
candidates.comment: A provider relation between a flight or parcel delivery and the organization that provides the service. Also called "provider", "airline", "delivery service". Examples: "Flight from London to NYC carrier British Airways", "Parcel delivery carrier FedEx".

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: arrivalGate
candidates.comment: An arrival gate relation between a flight and the identifier for its arrival gate. Also called gate number, landing gate. Examples: "A flight's arrival gate is 'Gate B23'.", "The flight's arrival gate is 'Terminal 1, Gate 15'."

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.justification: Inverse of isPartOf fits the subject-object relation.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

chosen_property.label: knows
chosen_property.justification: Knows fits the subject-object relation for Person to Person.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: knowsLanguage
candidates.comment: A language proficiency relation between an organization or person and a language they are able to communicate in. Also called speaks language, fluent in, understands language, conversant in. Examples: A person knowsLanguage 'English'. An organization knowsLanguage 'Spanish'. A diplomat knowsLanguage 'French' (fr).

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: transcript
candidates.comment: A transcript relation between an audio or video object and the text of its spoken content. Also called audio text, video text, spoken content. Examples: "AudioObject transcript 'Hello, welcome to the podcast.'", "VideoObject transcript 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'", "Lecture recording transcript 'Today we will discuss quantum physics.'".

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: language
candidates.comment: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: colleagues
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

chosen_property.label: trainedWith
chosen_property.definition: A person trains with another person.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: trainingSalary
candidates.comment: A training salary relation between an educational or work-based program and the estimated earnings during the program. Also called program salary, stipend, apprenticeship wage. Examples: "WorkBasedProgram trainingSalary '$25,000/year'", "EducationalOccupationalProgram trainingSalary '€1500/month'", "Apprenticeship trainingSalary '$12/hour'".

candidates.label: coach
candidates.comment: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".

candidates.label: exerciseRelatedDiet
candidates.comment: An exercise-related diet relation between an exercise action and the diet followed in conjunction with that action. Also called: workout diet, fitness diet, training nutrition. Examples: "Marathon Training" exercise related diet "High-Carb Diet", "Bodybuilding Workout" exercise related diet "High-Protein Diet", "Weight Loss Program" exercise related diet "Calorie-Restricted Diet".

candidates.label: course
candidates.comment: A location relation between an exercise action and the course where it was performed. Also called: exercise location, training course, activity venue. Examples: "Morning Run" course "Central Park Loop", "Golf Game" course "Augusta National", "Cycling Race" course "Tour de France Route".

candidates.label: instructor
candidates.comment: An instructional role relation between a course instance and the person who teaches or assists in teaching it. Also called teacher, lecturer, tutor, educator, faculty. Examples: A calculus course instance has 'Dr. Smith' as its instructor. A yoga class has 'Jane Doe' as its instructor. A coding bootcamp lists 'John Johnson' as an instructor.

candidates.label: exerciseCourse
candidates.comment: An exercise course relation between an exercise action and the specific place or course where the action was performed. Also called: workout location, training venue, activity course. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise course "Central Park Loop", "Swimming Practice" exercise course "Olympic Pool Lane 3", "Cycling Race" exercise course "Mountain Bike Trail". Distinct from fromLocation, which is the original location before the action.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: qualifications
candidates.comment: A qualification relation between a job posting or occupation and the specific credentials or skills required. Also called required skills, job requirements, eligibility criteria. Examples: "A software engineer job posting requires qualifications like a 'Bachelor's degree in Computer Science'.", "A doctor's occupation requires qualifications like 'Medical License'.", "A project manager role requires qualifications like 'PMP certification'."

candidates.label: proficiencyLevel
candidates.comment: A proficiency level relation between a technical article and the skill level required to understand its content. Also called skill level, required expertise, target audience level. Examples: "A Python tutorial has a proficiency level of 'Beginner'.", "A deep learning research paper has a proficiency level of 'Expert'.", "A guide to advanced calculus has a proficiency level of 'Intermediate'."
